rain.atmosphere: Rain must be visible in the air and in atmospheric attenuation, in addition to wet ground.
rain.camera: Sparse out-of-focus front-lens beads may provide local refraction, without screen-Y gravity rivulets: altitude gravity is perpendicular to the image plane.
rain.depth: Use approved second radial trial as reference. No central luminous hub, starburst or cluster; rain is less visible at center. Gradually longer inward-aligned soft drops away from center.
rain.intensity: Increase rain density, atmospheric attenuation and depth cues for heavier WMO rain intensities; moderate rain must remain distinguishable from a downpour.
rain.photography: Keep cinematic optical softness and restrained microcontrast; avoid a uniform rain texture overlay.
rain.direction: One invisible central vanishing point. At the center drops are end-on and less visible. Across all360degrees surrounding it, short drops aim slightly inward toward center; screen direction changes by quadrant.
rain.ground: For heavier rain, show distant-readable terrain effects: joined pools, active runoff, water sheen, wind/rain-ruffled water, reduced visibility. Scale effects plausibly to altitude; no gigantic individual ripple circles.

visual_rules.camera: Strict vertical90degree nadir; no sky or horizon.
visual_rules.landscapes: 120 different natural environments; temperature-appropriate vegetation and terrain.
visual_rules.photography: Cinematic film photographs with soft optical texture, atmospheric depth and restrained microcontrast.
visual_rules.clock: Naturally dark quiet upper-left region for white clock; no artificial dark overlay.

matrix.origin: custom collection using official Open-Meteo descriptions
matrix.contexts: day and night, each with two meteorologically plausible temperatures
